subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Retail Markup
description: A fast breakdown of The Retail Markup for builders.

hook.text: A café charges $5 for a latte. The raw beans cost about 10 cents. The cup costs more than the coffee.

buildup.text: Rent, labor, milk, equipment, and branding absorb most of that $5. The actual coffee is a tiny fraction.

discovery.text: In grocery retail, roasted coffee is marked up 100–300%. In cafés, the markup on raw beans exceeds 3,000%.

twist.text: Consumers pay for the experience, not the bean. A café's real product is atmosphere, convenience, and ritual.

climax.text: This disconnect means raising farmer prices by 50% would add pennies to a cup—but resistance remains.

punchline.text: You're buying the experience, not the bean. That's the markup.

quiz.question: What is the approximate markup on raw coffee beans in a café latte?
